gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The prediction identifies the same failed L2-error conversion in the Fourier approximation theorem: orthonormality and Parseval yield the Frobenius norm of the coefficient residual, while the available theorem controls only its max norm. Without a one-entry restriction, the dimension-dependent Frobenius-to-max conversion is required, so the dimension-free epsilon||A||_2 term is unsupported.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries diagnose the invalid replacement of the Fourier-polynomial L2 error, which equals ||A-EF*||_F, by the coefficient max norm. The missing factor sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)) prevents the max-norm matrix bound from establishing the claimed dimension-free L2 approximation term.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proof incorrectly converts the Fourier-polynomial L2 error, exactly equal to the coefficient residual Frobenius norm, into a max-norm bound without the dimension factor; consequently the dimension-free approximation term is not established.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states the erroneous max-norm inequality, derives the correct Frobenius identity from Parseval, notes the required sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)) conversion, and explains why the max-norm theorem cannot prove the claimed dimension-free L2 term.
